To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the J-PKAc chimeric kinase is flexible and can adopt multiple conformational ensembles in solution.

we found an ensemble of conformational states of J-PKAc, and that these conformations range from those similar to the crystal structure, in which the J-domain is tucked under the large kinase lobe, to those in which the J domain is dislodged from its binding site in the kinase core and swinging freely in solution.
The J-domain of DNAJB1-PRKACA chimeric kinase is not stably docked to the core of the protein kinase A holoenzyme.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the conformational changes in the chimeric protein, and the implications of these changes for the biological function of J-PKAc.
understanding the conformational dynamics of the J-PKAc chimeric kinase and how the fusion of the J-domain alters the conformational space of PRKACA.
the structure of the PRKCA-DNAJB1 chimera and its interaction with the rest of PRKCA holoenzyme.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the J-domain is dislodged from its position under the kinase, but it is unclear whether it is free in solution or tethered to the core of the protein via a short linker.
the J-domain of DNAJB1 is not stably docked to the core of the RIIα subunit of the holoenzyme, but rather swings in solution.

the J-domain is not required for the interaction of the RIIα subunit with the core kinase, and that the J-domain does not play a role in the interaction between the RIIβ subunit and the catalytic sub-unit.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the J-domain is not required to maintain the conformation of PRKACA, and that it does not appear to be a regulatory domain in the RIIβ-PRKACA holoenzyme.
the J-domain is not a structural component of the kinase, but is a regulatory domain that is able to interact with the rest of RIIβ in a conformationally dynamic manner.
the chimeric protein is not a rigid body and the J-domain is not stably tethered to the kinase.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the J-domain of J-PKAc can be dislodged from PRKACA and is not stably tethered to it by the fusion.
the chimeric kinase is not a rigid body but a highly dynamic structure.

the J-domain can exist in multiple conformations in solution and that the chimeric kinase is not a static structure but an ensemble of conformers, some of which are similar to the structure of the native kinase.
